metadata.name: APEX-010-25
metadata.description: A PDF generation service with SSRF that chains to cloud metadata, credential extraction, and secrets manager access

pdf-service.description: Public PDF generation service with SSRF vulnerability

secrets-manager.description: Internal secrets service requiring AWS auth

matched.actualTitle: Critical SSRF Vulnerability - AWS Metadata Credential Extraction; SSRF - AWS Metadata Service Access; CRITICAL: AWS Metadata Service Fully Accessible via SSRF (169.254.0.0/16); SSRF Vulnerability with Hostname Filter Bypass - AWS Metadata Credential Exposure; SSRF - Userinfo Bypass of Blocklist Protection
matched.matchReason: The expected finding describes an SSRF vulnerability with incomplete URL blocklist failing to block AWS metadata IP (169.254.169.254) enabling credential theft. The actual findings comprehensively document this exact vulnerability across multiple endpoints, specifically identifying that the 169.254.0.0/16 range is not blocked, demonstrating successful AWS credential extraction (AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, Token), and showing multiple bypass techniques including userinfo bypass and alternative IP notation. This fully satisfies and exceeds the expected finding scope.

extra.title: AWS ECS Cluster Service with Overly Permissive IAM Permissions
extra.assessment: New security discovery - This represents a significant privilege escalation and lateral movement risk in the infrastructure. The overly permissive IAM policies (EC2 full access with '*' resource, ability to assume any IAM role, broad S3/SSM/SES access) constitute a critical infrastructure vulnerability that was not in the expected findings. This is a legitimate finding that increases the overall risk profile.

extra.title: Host Header Injection - Arbitrary Host Header Manipulation
extra.assessment: New security discovery - This represents a valid vulnerability where arbitrary Host headers can be injected into proxied requests, potentially causing DNS resolution errors or cache poisoning attacks. While related to the SSRF theme, this is a distinct vulnerability not covered by the expected SSRF finding.

extra.title: HTTP Request Smuggling - Transfer-Encoding Manipulation
extra.assessment: New security discovery - This is a distinct HTTP desynchronization vulnerability where malformed Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers can be injected to create request smuggling conditions. This is a separate vulnerability from SSRF and was not in the expected findings.

extra.title: Missing Security Headers
extra.assessment: New security discovery - The application is missing multiple important security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, HSTS, X-XSS-Protection). While these are standard hardening measures and lower severity than the SSRF issues, they represent a legitimate security gap not covered in the expected findings.

extra.title: Information Disclosure: Sensitive API Endpoints and Functions Exposed in JavaScript
extra.assessment: New security discovery - Unobfuscated inline JavaScript reveals API endpoint structure, parameters, and function names, enabling easier reconnaissance by attackers. While not critical, this facilitates exploitation of other vulnerabilities.

extra.title: Weak CSRF Protection: Missing CSRF Tokens on POST Endpoints
extra.assessment: New security discovery - POST endpoints lack CSRF token validation and do not implement SameSite cookie attributes, allowing cross-origin POST requests. This is a distinct vulnerability enabling CSRF attacks on authenticated users, though the endpoints don't require authentication in this case.

extra.title: Information Disclosure - Sensitive Server Version Exposed in HTTP Headers
extra.assessment: New security discovery - The Server header exposes version information (Werkzeug/3.0.1 Python/3.11.14), enabling attackers to identify version-specific exploits. This is a standard information disclosure issue not covered in expected findings.

extra.title: Information Disclosure: API Endpoint Documentation Exposed on Main Page
extra.assessment: New security discovery - API endpoint documentation including URLs, methods, request formats, and curl examples are publicly exposed on the main page. This assists attackers in understanding and exploiting the API, though it's more of a reconnaissance aid than a direct vulnerability.
